info.title: Merran API
info.description: Everything the Merran app does, it does through this API: the same routes are open to scripts and to tools like Home Assistant. Tools use an API key: make one at `POST /api/auth/api-keys` while signed in, then send it as `Authorization: Bearer mrn_…`. Each route a key can use says which permission it needs, in `x-merran-permission` (like `recipes:read`); routes without it refuse keys. Browsers sign in with `POST /api/auth/sign-in/username` and send the session cookie it sets.

server.description: The address you reach Merran at

tags.name: Sign-in
tags.description: Setting up the server, signing in and out, invite links and switching households. Signed-in requests carry the session cookie.

tags.name: API keys
tags.description: Keys for scripts and tools like Home Assistant. Each acts as its person in one household, with only the permissions it was given, and stops working if it expires, is revoked, or its person leaves the household.

tags.name: Households
tags.description: The household in use: its settings, its people and their roles, and invite links.

tags.name: Recipes
tags.description: The household's recipes, their tags and versions, and Recently deleted. Ingredients and steps are written as lines, as in the editor, and each ingredient line is read into its amount, unit, food and note.

tags.name: Plan
tags.description: The week plan: meals on days and in the week's pool, what's next, and Fill the week's ideas, each saying why. Today is always the household's, in its time zone.

tags.name: List
tags.description: The shopping list, by aisle: from the plan (added up, and following the plan when meals change), typed in, or every week. Changes say what things were before, for Undo.

tags.name: Pantry
tags.description: What's at home, in the fridge, the freezer and the cupboard: what to use soon, and what's set aside for planned meals. Shopping put away goes in, and cooking a planned meal uses it up.

tags.name: Live
tags.description: What changes in the household, as it happens: the live updates the app uses, and who has the list open.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: Settings for the server (its admin only) and the household in use. A setting from an environment variable is locked, and a secret is never sent back: only whether it's set, and its last four characters.

get.description: Which of Merran's optional parts are on, what they make possible, and what the web app needs from them. Needs no sign-in: the web app reads it before anyone signs in.

Server-sent events for the household, for as long as the connection stays open:

- `ready` when it's open, with the areas it hears about.
- `plan`, `list`, `pantry`, `recipes` or `household` when something there changes, with who changed it (`by`). Fetch the area again to see what.
- `presence` with who has `page` open, when someone opens or leaves it.
- `ping` now and then, to keep the connection open.

A device that sends the same `client` with its own changes (in the `X-Merran-Client` header) isn't told about them; your other devices are. An API key hears about the areas it can read. With an API key, it needs the `any: read` permission.

post.summary: Change several things on the list at once
post.description: Take them off, check them off or not, move them to an aisle or another list (remembered for each food), or buy them every week: all or none. The answer says what they were before, for Undo with /list/restore. Ids not on the list are passed over. With an API key, it needs the `list: write` permission.

put.description: Household admins only. The lists as a whole, in order: one with no id is new, and one left out goes, with what's on it moving to the main list, which has to stay. post.summary: Put things on the list back as they were
post.description: Undo: items as taking them off or changing them said they were. One taken off comes back with its id. An aisle that's gone is left empty. With an API key, it needs the `list: write` permission.

A usual buy isn't offered again until it's next due. With an API key, it needs the `list: write` permission.

get.description: The fridge, the freezer and the cupboard: how much of each thing, its use-by date, the planned meals it's set aside for, and why to use it soon when it should be. With an API key, it needs the `pantry: read` permission.

patch.description: Move it (it goes after any dishes in its new slot), swap its recipe, give it a side, change its servings, or mark it planned, cooked or skipped. Cooked sets when its recipe and side were last made. With an API key, it needs the `plan: write` permission.

post.description: Makes another of your households the one in use on this device. Better Auth calls households organizations, so it's named by `organizationId`. An API key always works in its own household.

organizationSlug.description: The organization slug to set as active. It can be null to unset the active organization if organizationId is not provided. Eg: "org-slug"
